status_model.implemented: A reviewed bounded source anchor has a current Rust implementation and local source or test evidence; it is not a claim about the whole upstream member or allocator parity.
status_model.partial: Current Rust modules cover only the named source scope; unrepresented paths remain outside this row.
status_model.not-started: The named source scope has no current Rust engine module or evidence.
status_model.inapplicable: The named source scope is excluded from this private x86-64 engine evidence boundary; no Rust module or behavior claim is made.

overall.reason: A deterministic source map can record ownership and bounded implementation state, but it cannot establish full engine parity.
not_evidence: native C/Rust differential coverage for every mapped behavior
public C allocator API or runtime integration

units.source_scope: Owner-local free, live-owner cross-thread publication, and selected abandoned-page collection/reclaim transitions.
units.difference: The engine has bounded local, remote-free, and abandonment substrates. A 25-field native C/Rust differential proves two quiescent live-owner publications and owner-side collection; a separate 28-field native C/Rust differential proves real small direct-cache remote publication, owner collection, and exact reuse; an 8-field native C/Rust differential proves one arena-backed mapped page queue-detach, same-origin mi_free reclaim, re-association, and nonempty requeue; a separate 13-field native C/Rust differential proves the pinned C full-medium queue's unmapped abandonment and threshold reabandon while its Rust half executes one real bounded post-Theap-teardown route through the same sequential client-free threshold; an 18-field native C/Rust differential proves one real worker mi_thread_done followed by pthread join before consumer frees, selected mapped failed-reclaim/unown, and terminal release observations; a 21-field native C/Rust differential proves one real worker local mi_free retirement, real mi_thread_done plus join force-release of that retired page, then one distinct live-page mapped abandonment and consumer terminal free, with direct PageMap, ordinary arena bitmap, exact slice-span, and empty-route observations; a 25-field native C/Rust differential proves exactly two distinct live nonfull medium pages in distinct bins after a worker runs real mi_thread_done and the consumer calls pthread_join, then second-before-first consumer frees where only the second page terminally releases while the first remains PageMap-registered, arena-bitmap-set, mapped-abandoned, and used == 1 before its terminal free and empty route; a 46-field native C/Rust differential proves two distinct clients on one nonfull medium page A plus a one-client distinct-bin medium page B after a worker calls mi_thread_done(), returns, and the consumer calls pthread_join() before frees: A's first client returns StillLive while both pages and the route persist, B returns ReleasedPage while only B terminally releases, and A's second client returns ReleasedAll and completes the route; and a 53-field native C/Rust differential proves a same-bin two-page queue traversal after A fills, B is created, and A is restored to two clients: selected queue count/link/saved-successor state precedes mapped-abandoned count/bitmap transitions 2 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0 through A StillLive, B ReleasedPage, and A ReleasedAll. A separate 40-field native C/Rust differential fills one 1025-byte ordinary regular-small arena page (1280-byte class, 51 blocks, one slice), locally retires it at 16, lets the next generic same-Theap allocation quick-collect and reuse a just-freed block on the same page, then force-collects queue/PageMap/arena-bitmap/slice release. None proves general asynchronous public free routing, retirement, teardown, abandonment/adoption, concurrent collection, or general thread exit.

units.source_scope: Selected external-arena metadata, ordinary and direct-cache page-area commitment, page registration, mapped abandonment/reclaim, and exact release paths.
units.difference: Rust supports bounded caller-supplied arena ownership and selected release transitions. An 8-field native C/Rust differential additionally proves one arena-backed mapped-abandon bitmap transition followed by same-origin nonempty reclaim and requeue. A distinct 13-field C/Rust differential observes pinned C initially-unmapped source abandonment and threshold-driven mapped bitmap publication while its Rust half executes one real bounded post-Theap-teardown route through the same transition and eventual terminal release. A further 18-field C/Rust differential observes one worker Theap/TLD teardown followed by pthread join, selected mapped failed-reclaim/unown, and terminal checks `page_map_unregistered_after_final_free`, `arena_page_bitmap_clear_after_final_free`, and `arena_slice_released_after_final_free`. A completed 21-field C/Rust differential observes one worker local mi_free retirement, real mi_thread_done plus join force-release of that retired page, then a distinct live page's mapped abandonment and one consumer terminal free with `page_map_unregistered_after_final_free`, `arena_page_bitmap_clear_after_final_free`, `arena_slice_released_after_final_free`, and an empty route. A separate 25-field C/Rust differential records exactly two distinct live nonfull medium arena pages in distinct bins after a worker runs real mi_thread_done and the consumer calls pthread_join: both are mapped-abandoned, then the second page alone unregisters from the PageMap, clears its ordinary arena bitmap, and releases its exact slice span while the first remains registered, bit-set, mapped-abandoned, and used == 1 until its terminal release and empty route. A separate 46-field C/Rust differential records two distinct clients on one nonfull medium page A plus a one-client distinct-bin medium page B after a worker calls mi_thread_done(), returns, and the consumer calls pthread_join() before frees: A's first client returns StillLive while both arena memberships and the route persist, B returns ReleasedPage and releases only B, and A's second client returns ReleasedAll and completes the route. A separate 53-field C/Rust differential records same-bin A/B queue count/link/saved-successor traversal after A fills, B is created, and A is restored to two clients, then mapped-abandoned count/bitmap transitions 2 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0 through StillLive, ReleasedPage, and ReleasedAll. A separate 40-field C/Rust differential fills one 1025-byte ordinary regular-small arena page (1280-byte class, 51 blocks, one slice), locally retires it at 16, quick-collects/reuses a just-freed same-page block through the next generic same-Theap allocation, then force-collects its queue/PageMap/ordinary arena bitmap/exact slice release. A separate 23-field C/Rust differential begins one reserved medium page with the fixed four-OS-page prefix, exhausts it, directly commits its next page area before ordinary free-list extension and same-page reuse, then force-collects its final release. Only its pinned C oracle sets `mi_option_page_commit_on_demand`; Rust uses a private `cfg(test)` seam. On direct-commit failure that seam deliberately returns None and preserves the selected page for an explicit retry, whereas upstream `src/page.c:845-863` may retire and fall through to fresh allocation; this intentional test-only divergence is recorded in `known-differences.md`, not C fault-injection parity. A separate 44-field C/Rust differential begins one reserved 1024-byte small direct-cache page with the same four-OS-page prefix, exhausts eight direct objects, extends to sixteen without another mapping after allocation nine, then grows the prefix to eight OS pages before the allocation-seventeen extension to twenty-four. Its complete direct-cache image, queue, PageMap, arena bit, payload, and forced normal release are checked; source anchors establish commit-before-extension while the trace is only a poststate witness. It does not map Rust option parsing/API/policy, a fresh fallback, or C fault-injection parity. Registry-wide reservation, multi-arena policy, general retirement/teardown, general abandonment/adoption, and general thread teardown remain absent.
